A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FedALS and generalization-bound study. Their complete main texts, Figures 1–3, Tables 1–3, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-classification and language-model experiments, communication measurements, and parameter analyses in Section 7 and Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including benchmark comparisons and analyses of aggregation frequency and model partitioning.

M1.justification: Core FedALS in Algorithm 1 is unchanged. However, Algorithm 4 revises FedALS + SCAFFOLD: the gradient correction uses mean rather than summed controls, and both partition-specific control updates reverse their local/global control terms. These change the specified procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate image classification on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN, and MNIST, and OPT-125M fine-tuning on MultiNLI, retaining the same iid and non-iid scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Table 1 and Figures 2–3 is unchanged. Nevertheless, Appendix D revises the specified SCAFFOLD baseline in Algorithm 3 by averaging global controls and changing the control-update signs. The PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation design retains five clients, the same data partitioning, ResNet-20 and OPT-125M configurations, batch sizes of 64 and 16, optimizers, learning-rate search, and evaluation metrics. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: The layerwise consensus-distance analysis in Figure 1, aggregation-coefficient and communication analysis in Table 2, and representation/head partition analysis in Table 3 are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Both versions explicitly report 20 repetitions per experiment and means with standard-deviation error bars. v3 relocates this disclosure without changing the statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: The reported curves and all entries in Tables 1–3 are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains FedALS non-iid SVHN accuracy of 0.8117 ± 0.0214 and non-iid MultiNLI test loss of 1.2773 ± 0.0019.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.3 replaces the sample-based gradient-variance condition with a population-expectation condition, also stated in Theorem B.2. Appendix B corrects the dataset used in the optimization-error definition and sampling exponents from n_k to |Z_k,r|. The principal bound formulas and proof strategies remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The conclusion removes its explicit claim of being first to derive an R-round bound for heterogeneous data. This is a limited change in stated novelty: Section 4 retains broader first-in-the-literature wording, and the abstract and other contribution claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix C now states that the partial-participation out-of-sample gap can be bounded using both Theorems 4.1 and 4.3; v1 referred only to the one-round Theorem A.2. This modestly expands stated applicability. The empirical interpretations and aggregation-versus-optimization limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 removes Section 7's Ubuntu 20.04, Intel Core i9-10980XE, and five GeForce RTX 2080 hardware disclosure. This reduces reproducibility information; it does not establish that the hardware actually changed.

R1.justification: The bibliography is unchanged. Section 4.1 adds Sun and Yagli to its direct comparison alongside Barnes, although both were already cited elsewhere. Section 4.2 removes the explicit contrast that Barnes lacks representation learning and instead cites similarity in the averaged generalization measure.

P1.justification: v3 corrects the author email, grammar, terminology, and theorem references, adds a pointer to the existing Theorem 4.3 proof, and trims several short passages. The section and appendix organization remains substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 uses larger type and moves from page 8 to page 9, while Tables 2–3 use smaller type. Figures remain unchanged. Limited mathematical reformatting includes a newly malformed expectation subscript in Appendix C.

improvement.justification: The control-variable corrections in Algorithms 3–4 and the corrected sample references in Appendix B improve the precision of the algorithmic and mathematical specifications. These limited gains outweigh the removed hardware disclosure and the new Appendix C typesetting defect. The revision does not establish a substantial improvement to the paper's unchanged empirical evidence or central theoretical results.
